transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Lumera Head of ML), Rajiv Kapoor (Lumera CTO), Aisha Brown (Lumera Product)

Summary (auto):
- Goal: Scope a 4-week POC to evaluate open models for customer-facing medical triage and summarization use cases.
- Discussed shortlist of open models, quality vs cost tradeoffs, multilingual needs (EN + ES), domain adaptation, benchmarks, and timeline.
- Agreed next steps: send shortlist + perf matrix, share benchmark harness, Lumera to provide samples and success criteria.

Topics: model shortlist; latency & throughput targets; quality & hallucination tolerance; evaluation metrics (EM, Rouge, factuality); privacy/data handling (KMS, SOC2); timeline & scope for 4-week POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick intros?
[00:08] Maya: hi, maya here, head of ml at lumera, mostly running ingestion and models for our clinician-facing features.
[00:14] Rajiv: rajiv — cto, i'll be involved on infra and compliance side.
[00:18] Aisha: aisha, product — i'll represent success criteria from the product side.
[00:22] Diego: diego, solutions engineer, i'll handle the benchmark runs and perf questions.
[00:27] Samira: great. quick framing — you're looking for a POC to evaluate open models for triage chat and note summarization, with some multilingual needs?
[00:36] Maya: yeah that's right. Two primary flows: 1) live chat triage where latency needs to be low — p95 ideally under 2s for short replies; 2) batch summarization of patient notes where throughput matters more than single-request latency. Also both en and spanish for a subset of users.
[00:55] Rajiv: and because we're healthcare, data never leaves our VPC in production; for the POC we can use anonymized samples but we need to validate KMS and audit logging. SOC 2 posture is a must.
[01:06] Samira: totally — we'll include our private options and KMS notes in the security packet. for model choices we typically recommend a short list of open models with a mix of sizes and quantization profiles so you can see tradeoffs.

[01:20] Diego: quick question on traffic patterns — what's expected qps for the triage flow?
[01:24] Maya: initial is small, ~50 rps peak, but realistic POC target is to show we can handle 200 req/min steady with bursts; most requests are short (1-2 sentences).
[01:34] Diego: ok that's helpful. for throughput tests we'll do sustained runs and some burst tests.

[01:45] Aisha: success criteria from product — for triage: p95 under 2s, accuracy of triage decision within 92% versus our annotators, false positives low; for summarization: clinician-rated quality >=4/5 on a small eval set and ROUGE-L > x (we'll provide thresholds).

[02:05] Samira: noted. now on models — our shortlist for open-model POCs usually includes: Llama 3 (instruct variants), Mistral (7B and Mixtral 8x), Falcon 40B, and a distilled Falcon/quantized Falcon like gptq variants; we can also include OpenAssistant-style instruction-tuned weights for safety; any preferences?
[02:28] Maya: we want strong medical grounding — hallucination risk is biggest concern. we've seen Llama2 earlier underperform on clinical abbreviations. is Llama 3 better?
[02:38] Diego: Llama 3 shows improvement on instruction-following and factuality in public benchmarks, but depending on quantization you might lose some fidelity. mixtral/mistral variants tend to be cost-efficient and surprisingly good on multilingual.
[02:50] Rajiv: what about Falcon 40B — big model, higher cost, but better out-of-the-box factuality?
[02:56] Samira: falcon 40B is solid for few-shot and can be strong on technical text; it's heavier so latency/cost tradeoff is real unless you use dedicated GPUs and good batching. for POC we typically test 7B-13B-sized cheap configs + one 40B as a high-quality baseline.
[03:10] Maya: multilingual — spanish support is non-negotiable; we also have some triage notes in spanish and code-switching. which of those models handle spanish well?
[03:19] Diego: Mistral/Mixtral have good multilingual performance in the 7–8B class; Llama 3 shows improvements too. we should include an ES-specific eval set.
[03:27] Aisha: domain adapt — do you recommend fine-tuning or RAG with vector DB + retrieval?
[03:32] Samira: usually start with retrieval-augmented prompts (RAG) using an embeddings model + small context window; for heavy domain needs a light finetune or instruction-tune can help. for healthcare, retrieval reduces hallucination if the index is good and you control snippets.
[03:45] Maya: can you do retrieval within the POC or is that separate?
[03:48] Diego: we can include a retrieval baseline — we'll ask for sample docs to build the vector store. latency implications: retrieval adds overhead but can be cached for common queries.
[03:58] Rajiv: security — are any of these models available in a private deployment option so data never leaves our cloud?
[04:03] Samira: yes — Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted inference and customer-managed KMS. for the POC we can run in a shared Redwood-hosted environment with anonymized data if you prefer faster setup; if you want VPC we'll scope additional infra lead time.
[04:18] Rajiv: lead time?
[04:20] Samira: about 2-3 weeks to spin up a private deployment depending on region and procurement; hosted POC can start in 3-5 business days once NDA and sample data are ready.
[04:32] Maya: timeline-wise we want a 4-week POC: week 0 scoping and data prep, week 1 baseline runs, week 2 tuning + retrieval tests, week 3 final runs and evaluation. realistic?
[04:44] Diego: yes that's our typical cadence. we'll need 2-3 hours with your team at the start to align eval scripts.
[04:51] Aisha: what's the benchmark suite look like?
[04:54] Diego: we'll run: latency p50/p95, throughput sustained, ROUGE for summaries, custom accuracy for triage decisions (we'll map labels), factuality checks using automated metrics plus small human eval, and hallucination spot checks. we'll provide the harness and you can run locally or we can run and share logs.
[05:12] Samira: cost/quantization conversation: we can show int8/gptq profiles that reduce memory and cost but sometimes harm accuracy slightly; we'll include both float16 and quantized runs.
[05:24] Maya: how do you compare cost across models?
[05:26] Samira: we'll produce cost-per-1k-tokens and cost-per-request estimates based on your expected payload distribution; we'll also show dedicated vs hosted numbers.
[05:35] Rajiv: any regulatory red flags for PII in sample data? we will scrub identifiers but maintain clinical content.
[05:41] Diego: fine — we prefer fully anonymized data for hosted runs; for anything with PHI we recommend private deployment and ensure KMS/HSM options. we'll put that in the security doc.
[05:52] Aisha: are you going to run an LLM hallucination regression test? we have some legal concerns about bad summaries.
[05:58] Samira: yes we'll include a targeted hallucination test set and threshold gating. if a model fails the gating we can try retrieval or a different model.
[06:06] Maya: curious about evaluation size — how many examples do you need?
[06:09] Diego: for initial automated metrics 500 examples per task is a good start; for human evaluation 50-100 examples per model gives directional signal.
[06:18] Rajiv: ok. budget question — we may prefer cheaper 7B models if accuracy loss is acceptable. can we get a perf/quality curve?
[06:26] Samira: yes that's exactly what we'll send — perf/quality/cost curves across selected model+quant combos.
[06:31] Aisha: any integrations we should prepare? e.g., SSO or audit log hooks?
[06:36] Diego: we support SAML/SSO and can forward audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3; we'll include integration notes.
[06:45] Samira: next, any blockers on your side for datasets and legal?
[06:48] Maya: legal confirmed anonymized dataset ok for hosted POC. secondary question: data residency — can you keep data in us-east only?
[06:55] Samira: yes we can pin region; we'll confirm in the security doc.
[06:59] Rajiv: great. on success criteria recap — p95 < 2s for triage, throughput target 200 req/min, accuracy ~92% triage, clinician-rated summary >=4/5.
[07:12] Samira: captured. we'll produce an initial project plan and a model shortlist email.
[07:16] Aisha: timeframe for the checklist & model list?
[07:18] Samira: i'll send model shortlist + perf matrix by 2025-04-14; diego will share harness link by 2025-04-12.
[07:25] Maya: please include Spanish eval set example.
[07:28] Diego: will do.
[07:30] (brief cross talk, someone mutes/unmutes)
[07:40] Samira: any competitor concerns? you mentioned you're evaluating vendor options?
[07:44] Rajiv: we're also talking to OpenAI for hosted LLM + Anthropic for safety features, but open-model path preferable for cost and control.
[07:53] Samira: understood. for the POC we'll make sure cost comparisons are apples-to-apples with throughput and latency targets.
[07:59] Aisha: ok, if we get the sample data to you Monday, when would you start?
[08:04] Diego: we could kick off baseline runs mid next week — assuming harness access and data arrive Mon/Tue.
[08:12] Samira: cool. final recap: Samira sends shortlist, Diego shares harness, Lumera provides data and success criteria doc, schedule benchmark kickoff (week of 2025-04-14).
[08:25] Maya: thanks — that works.
[08:27] Rajiv: thanks everyone.
[08:30] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up over email with links and timelines.

End of transcript.

Notes on model shortlist (auto):
- Llama 3 instruct (13B and 7B variants) — expected strong instruction following; may need domain tuning for medical abbreviations.
- Mistral / Mixtral (7B/8B) — good cost-to-quality, strong multilingual.
- Falcon 40B — high-quality baseline, cost/latency heavier.
- Quantized GPTQ variants — cost-efficient experiments for latency/throughput.
- Retrieval + smaller model baseline recommended to reduce hallucinations.

Attachments/links referenced:
- Benchmark harness repo (to be shared by Diego)
- Security & SOC2 brief (Samira to attach)
